id: HWE2: spurious estimate under the robot's own arm motion on the real G1, no push (C8)
registered: 2026-11-13, before any arm-motion recording with the load cell. Simulation reference ESTCMP2 (registered): peak spurious estimate ours / centroidal + IMU = gesture 6-8 / 16-17, lift 17-23 / 24-26, jab 45-52 / 53-55, swing 39-63 / 42-81 N.
setup: as HWE1 (FALCON stands, shadow), arms driven by a scripted replay of the simulation comparison's retargeted ACCAD clips (amendment 1). Load cell held by nobody; the stick rests on the floor. Ground truth = 0 external force.
sessions: two sessions (same as HWE1). Motions gesture, lift, jab, swing = the ESTCMP2 clips (motions/accad_upper_only.pkl keys of run_ffk.sh), exported unchanged to motions/hwe2_arm_clips.npz. Per motion and session one recording of 5 repetitions: experiments/claude_brace/arm_replay_bridge.py --clips motions/hwe2_arm_clips.npz --motion <m> (speed and options per amendment 2; 3 s still before, per repetition a smooth ramp from the standing arm pose to the clip start, the clip, a ramp back, 4 s still) with deploy_real.py --init_ctrl falcon --shadow ... --fs_upper xr (40 repetitions).
window: a repetition = arm joint speed norm > 0.5 rad/s, merged within 0.3 s, window extended by 0.3 s on both sides; excluded if a foot lifts (FALCON step) or the load cell exceeds 2 N in the window (decided without estimates).
metric: peak |xy estimate - median of the 1 s before the window| inside the window, per estimator.

predictions.A1 (primary): peak spurious estimate: centroidal + IMU (CIMU) higher than ours, paired one-sided Wilcoxon over all included repetitions, alpha 0.05; requires >= 20 repetitions, otherwise inconclusive.
predictions.reported: per motion type medians for all five estimators; repetitions above the 25 N hold-entry threshold per estimator; kappa fit of the peak against the arm inertial force if the arm accelerations are available.

analysis: hw_arm_sync.py (hashed in CRITERIA_HWE2.sha256 before the first arm-motion session); the replay tool arm_replay_bridge.py and the clip file are hashed there as well before the first counted recording.
amendment 1: 2026-11-13, robot PC, before any arm-motion recording counts: XR teleoperation replaced by the scripted replay (reproducible repetitions with exact still holds, same motions as the simulation reference). Window, exclusions, metric, A1 and the analysis code (hw_arm_sync.py, hashed) are unchanged. Known differences to the simulation: the FALCON stand (not our controller) holds the robot, and deploy_real --fs_upper limits each arm joint to 1.5 rad/s (the lift clip reaches 4.1 rad/s, so it plays slower on hardware); the kappa fit uses the measured arm angles. Disclosure: one XR-teleoperated practice recording (g1lc_20261113_170156_s1_arm_gesture, no 3 s stills, 5 merged repetitions) was analysed with hw_arm_sync.py before this amendment (CIMU - ours median -0.9 N, n 5); it is excluded from every decision.
amendment 2: 2026-11-13, robot PC with the dev PC, before the first counted arm-motion recording. (a) Speeds: the --fs_upper limit of 1.5 rad/s clips each joint separately (distorts and delays the motion), so every clip is slowed uniformly to stay inside it: gesture 0.79 (first 6 s of the 50.7 s clip, --clip_s 6), lift 0.36, jab 0.45, swing 1.0 (whole clips otherwise); reference peak joint speed 1.00 / 1.48 / 1.49 / 1.21 rad/s. Ramps between the standing pose and the clip are lengthened to <= 1 rad/s. (b) swing: both shoulder rolls 0.1 rad outward (--roll_out 0.1): in the model the left wrist enters the left hip by 1.7 cm (32 of 172 frames); 0.05 rad already clears it. The other clips have no arm contact and stay in the joint range. (c) The speed (and roll offset) is part of the recording label, e.g. s1_arm_jab_sp045. (d) Interpretation fixed in advance: in simulation the gap between ours and centroidal + IMU grew with speed (1.5-2x) and was small at 1x (jab 45-52 vs 53-55 N); hardware runs slower than 1x, so A1 may come out inconclusive or not met. That would not overturn the simulation result C8 (shown for fast motions); it would mean the two estimators are similar at the slow end on hardware.
amendment 3: 2026-11-13, robot PC, after the first scripted recording (g1lc_20261113_172010_s1_arm_gesture_sp079): the operator saw the hands touch the body. Measured on hardware, the wrists sag 0.27-0.31 rad (pitch) and the elbows / shoulders 0.04-0.06 rad below the command (low arm gains, Dex3 hand weight), so the left wrist reached the left hip. With that sag added to the clips (contact check in the model, measured FALCON leg posture), gesture comes to 0.4 cm and swing penetrates 2.2 cm; lift and jab keep > 5 cm. Fix: gesture --pitch_up 0.15 --roll_out 0.1 (> 5 cm), swing --pitch_up 0.35 --roll_out 0.15 (4.5 cm; replaces the 0.1 roll of amendment 2); lift and jab unchanged. Offsets go into the label. The recording 172010 is excluded (arm-body contact, decided from the operator's observation and the kinematics, before its estimates were looked at).
amendment 4: 2026-11-13, robot PC, before any estimate of a scripted recording was looked at (only window counts and times). The speed rule of 'window' (|dq_arm| > 0.5 rad/s merged within 0.3 s) splits a slowed clip into many pieces (gesture: 18 windows for 5 repetitions; with 2 s merging still 8), because the slowed arms often move below 0.5 rad/s inside a repetition; the 1 s baseline then falls inside the same repetition. For the scripted replay a repetition is instead the time the arms are away from their standing pose: max joint deviation > 0.05 rad from the median arm pose of 0.5-2.5 s into the recording (before the replay starts), merged within 1 s, at least 0.5 s, extended by 0.3 s (hw_arm_sync.py --window pose, the default; --window speed keeps the original rule). Exclusions, baseline, metric and A1 unchanged. Result on session 1: one window per repetition (gesture 5, lift 3 + 3, jab 5, swing 5).
amendment 5: 2026-11-13, robot PC, bug fix after the pooled run: each repetition was replayed from 3 s before it (2 s warm-up + 1 s baseline), but the warm-up is counted as 400 ticks and the decimated ticks average 5.0 ms with jitter, so the valid replay began ~5 ms after the baseline start and the first baseline tick was missing in a tick-phase-dependent subset ('no baseline': 9 of 45 repetitions). The replay now starts 0.5 s earlier; window, exclusions, metric and A1 are unchanged. The pooled run before the fix (A1: n 33, median +1.6 N, 21/33, p 0.045) is kept in hwe2_results_prefix.json and reported alongside.

amendment 6 (HWE2b).id: HWE2 amendment 6 = HWE2b (DRAFT, dev PC 2026-11-16, for the robot PC to register before the first HWE2b recording): the HWE2 arm-motion test re-recorded with OUR controller standing and driving the arms
amendment 6 (HWE2b).registered_HWE2_result_kept: HWE2 (FALCON stand, amendments 1-5) stays reported as registered: peaks ours 43.2 / MOB 18.6 / CIMU 39.9 N, A1 not met (25/42, p 0.091). HWE2b does not replace it; both are reported.
amendment 6 (HWE2b).reason: Found after the HWE2 results (disclosed as such): in HWE2 the FALCON policy drove the arms with 50 Hz step-wise commands (change interval median 18.7 ms, step p99 0.067 rad) and the pelvis IMU above 15 Hz was 5-10x quiet stance during arm motion; at the registered bandwidth (K = 100 1/s) both IMU-resolved estimates passed this vibration. The simulation reference ESTCMP2 has our controller standing and tracking the arm reference. Open question: is the vibration the policy's step commands or the robot's own compliance? (Simulation with 50 Hz step references, RA_UM_ZOH = 0.02, did NOT reproduce the hardware ranking, so the command hypothesis is not established.) HWE2b answers it on hardware.
amendment 6 (HWE2b).setup: deploy_real.py --stage R2 with S21z2 WITHOUT --steps and --upper xr (HWE2b_config_S21z2.txt, hashed below; the draft named S21p - the hardware controller moved to S21z2 on 11-17 before any HWE2b recording, it keeps the S21p stance/hold and adds the in-hold estimate and release fixes). The arm-pause options (RA_UM_PAUSE*) are not used: they would change the arm motion at every hold entry. Arms follow arm_replay_bridge.py with the same clips, speeds, offsets as amendments 2-3; labels get the suffix _b. Load cell resting on the floor (ground truth 0).
amendment 6 (HWE2b).amount: per motion and session one recording of 5 repetitions, two sessions (40 repetitions), as HWE2; >= 20 included repetitions required for A1/A2, otherwise inconclusive.
amendment 6 (HWE2b).window_exclusions_metric: unchanged: amendment-4 pose window, exclusions (a foot lifts, or the load cell > 2 N in the window), baseline = median of the 1 s before the window, metric = peak |xy estimate - baseline|. Added exclusion (decided without estimates): a guard trip or a SafetyGate stop inside the window. Hold-first entries are NOT an exclusion (the entry is decided by our own estimate); their number per estimator setting is reported.
amendment 6 (HWE2b).estimates: all estimators recomputed offline by the hashed hw_arm_sync.py replay from the recorded lowstate, exactly as in HWE2 (the live controller's estimate is not used).

predictions.A1 (primary, unchanged): peak spurious estimate: CIMU higher than ours at the registered bandwidth (K = 100 1/s), paired one-sided Wilcoxon, alpha 0.05.
predictions.A2 (secondary, matched latency; the meth: with IMU-SME and CIMU refiltered at K' = 25 1/s (hwe2_posthoc_e2.py; matched E1 delay50 57.2 / 57.7 / 57.9 ms ours / MOB / CIMU) and MOB as registered: ours < MOB and ours < CIMU, each a paired one-sided Wilcoxon, alpha 0.05 (both required).
predictions.V (mechanism check, reported): pelvis IMU power above 15 Hz during arm motion relative to the 1 s quiet baseline, HWE2b vs HWE2 per motion. If it is not lower than in HWE2 (median ratio > 0.5), the vibration is the robot's compliance, not the policy's commands; A1/A2 are interpreted with that.
predictions.reported: per motion medians for all estimators at K = 100 and K' = 25; repetitions above the 25 N hold-entry threshold; hold-first entries during arm motion (live controller, RA2E_MOT_K on).

amendment 6 (HWE2b).analysis: hw_arm_sync.py (hashed, unchanged) for A1; hwe2_posthoc_e2.py with KS=100,25 for A2 (hash it with this amendment before the first HWE2b recording).
amendment 6 (HWE2b).registered: 2026-11-17, robot PC, before the first HWE2b recording (from the dev-PC draft CRITERIA_HWE2_AMENDMENT6_HWE2b_DRAFT.json).

amendment 7 (HWE2b controller): 2026-11-17, robot PC, before any HWE2b recording with S21z4. HWE2b session 1 under S21z2 (amendment 6): the gesture recording (g1lc_20261117_125502) completed and stays an S21z2 result; the lift and jab recordings were stopped by the raw-estimate guard outside hold (own arm motion drove the deployed estimate to 800-1500 N) and the two earlier lift/jab attempts had no arm motion (arm-reference reader did not reopen) - none of them counts. From now on the controller is S21z4 (HWE2b_config_S21z4.txt, hashed): S21z2 + RA_HOLD_LEGPD=0.15, RA_FZMIN=0.2 (r2_flags), RA_IMU_DRATE=10000, RA2E_MOT_K=25,0.05,0.5,70, DEPLOY_GUARD_EST_NS=0; the ArmRefReader reopen is in the code (10d6035). All four motions are recorded under S21z4 in sessions 1 and 2 (the S21z2 gesture is reported separately). Window, exclusions, metric, A1 / A2 / V and the analysis are unchanged. Note for the interpretation: the deployed estimate is not used by the analysis (offline replay of the registered estimators), but RA2E_MOT_K now raises the hold-entry threshold to 70 N while the arms are commanded to move, which changes how often hold-first runs during the repetitions (reported).
amendment 8 (HWE2b controller, FZMIN): 2026-11-17, robot PC, before any HWE2b recording under amendment 7: RA_FZMIN=0.2 (r2_flags of amendment 7) is removed -> 0.1 (R2 default) because on hardware it tipped short lateral pushes of 37/42 N to the 15 deg guard, while with 0.1 short pushes up to 70 N held (robot_pc_reports/2026-11-17/s21z4). Controller = HWE2b_config_S21z4b.txt (hashed; identical to S21z4 except that flag). No recording was made under amendment 7. Everything else unchanged.
